article: Edge AI and NPU architecture: tradeoffs, designs, and model optimization
findings: Read the full Japanese article and all twelve translations; preserved the original publication date and set lastmod to 2026-11-23 in every edition.
Reframed cloud latency as route-, load-, and server-dependent, required end-to-end measurement, and warned against relying on one AI prediction for safety-critical control.
Clarified that on-device processing can reduce raw-data transmission but does not guarantee privacy or security; corrected NPU capability and GPU/NPU comparison claims.

Removed universal MAC-array, Tensor Core, SRAM, and DRAM-energy claims; qualified product examples, corrected the Google Tensor/Edge TPU relationship, and removed stale Apple and Snapdragon performance claims.

Explained that quantization, pruning, distillation, and execution-provider portability have model-, runtime-, and hardware-dependent effects; no speed, accuracy, or universal-optimum guarantee is made.
Aligned the single Mermaid dataflow diagram across all thirteen editions and checked all nine official source URLs for HTTP 200.
scope: Complete Japanese source and twelve translations. Meaning, terminology, product distinctions, optimization limits, links, and one Mermaid diagram checked. AI review only; publication is still pending.

meaning.note: Compared the complete edition with the Japanese source: cloud/on-device choice and variable end-to-end latency; privacy/security limits of local processing; NPU inference/training and operator support; heterogeneous CPU/GPU/NPU execution and benchmark conditions; architecture and data-movement tradeoffs; Apple Core ML, Google Tensor versus Cloud/Edge TPU, and Qualcomm examples; quantization, pruning, and distillation caveats; hybrid deployment, portability, and conclusion.

terminology.note: Checked localized usage of edge/on-device/cloud inference, accelerator/NPU, CPU/GPU, MAC, systolic array, product-specific Tensor Core, TOPS, runtime/execution provider, quantization, sparsity/pruning, and knowledge distillation.

mathematics.note: No mathematical formulas, derivations, or numeric performance claims remain. TOPS appears as a peak-throughput label whose limits are explicitly explained.

code.note: Compared the one Mermaid MAC/dataflow diagram in all thirteen editions: node and edge identifiers match. There is no executable article code; the diagram was checked structurally but not rendered or visually inspected.

links.note: All editions use the same nine primary-source URLs: Apple Core ML performance analysis, compute units and model compression; ONNX Runtime quantization and Execution Providers; Qualcomm Hexagon and AI Engine; Google Pixel Tensor G6 announcement; and Coral Edge TPU documentation. Each URL returned HTTP 200 during this review.

post/edge-ai-npu-architecture/index.en.m.summary: Corrected overgeneralized claims about cloud latency, local privacy, NPU/GPU efficiency, universal NPU training, memory architecture, product lineage, quantization/pruning/distillation outcomes, and one-write portability; added current primary references and aligned all sections with the Japanese source.
limitations: AI review only; no human or native-speaker certification.
No NPU model was run or benchmarked on physical devices; end-to-end performance is guidance for readers to measure on their own target hardware.
The Mermaid diagram was structurally compared but not rendered or visually inspected.
No local Hugo full build was run; run the repository CI build and verify all thirteen rendered pages after deployment.
Vendor product capabilities and documentation can change; model, runtime, hardware, and OS compatibility should be rechecked for a concrete deployment.
